Abu al-Hasan al-Mawardi informed me, saying: Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, saying: Aslam al-Ma'arri narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Muzzammil, hardship will be lifted from him in this world and the Hereafter" [41] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/157.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

﴿O you who wrap yourself in garments!﴾ Al-Muzzammil, the one wrapped in his garment. Its origin is al-mutazammil, and the ta' was assimilated into the za'. Similarly it is said: tazammal and tadaththar bi-thawbihi when one covers oneself with it, and zammala ghayrahu when one covers another.

Imru' al-Qays said:

"A great man of the people in a coarse cloak, wrapped up"

[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/255.]]

Abu Abdullah al-Jadali said: I asked Aisha about His words, glorified is He: "O you who wrap yourself in garments!" What was that wrapping? She said: It was a woolen cloak whose length was fourteen cubits; half of it was over me while I slept, and half of it was over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he prayed.

Abu Abdullah said: So I asked her what it was made of.

She said: By Allah, it was neither combed wool, nor silk, nor fleece, nor brocade, nor wool; its warp was hair and its weft was wool.

Al-Suddi said: He meant: O you who sleep, arise and pray. Ikrimah said: That is, O you who has taken upon himself this matter, i.e., bears it. He used to read "al-Muzzammal" with a light za' and an open mim and a doubled one. The wise said: He addressed him as "al-Muzzammil" and "al-Muddaththir" at the beginning because he had not yet delivered anything of the message.

﴿Stand [in prayer] through the night﴾ — the common reading is with a kasra on the mim (qum), while Abu al-Sammak al-Adawi read it with a damma on it, following the damma of the qaf. ﴿except a little﴾ — then He explained: ﴿half of it, or reduce it a little, or add to it, and recite the Qur'an distinctly﴾ — giving him a choice among these stages. When this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions prayed, and it was difficult for them, for a man did not know when a third of the night was, or when half was, or two-thirds, so he would stand until morning for fear of not keeping track. This became hard on them, their feet swelled and their complexions changed. So Allah had mercy on them, lightened it for them, and abrogated it with His words: ﴿He knows that there will be among you those who are ill﴾ [[Surah al-Muzzammil: 20.]] to the end of the verse. Between the beginning of the surah and its end was a year.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When His words were revealed, "O you who wrap yourself in garments!", the Prophet (ﷺ) remained in this state for ten years, standing in the night as Allah had commanded him, and a group of his companions would stand with him. Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed after ten years: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than two-thirds of the night﴾ [[Surah al-Muzzammil: 20.]] to the end of the verse. So He lightened it for them after ten years.

Muqatil and Ibn Kaysan said: This was before the five daily prayers were prescribed, and then it was abrogated by the five prayers. Ibn Abbas said: When the beginning of al-Muzzammil was revealed, they would stand in prayer about as much as they did in Ramadan, and between its beginning and its end was a year.

Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Aisha, who said:

I used to make a mat for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to pray on at night. People heard of it and gathered; when their numbers increased, he disliked that and feared it would be made obligatory upon them to pray at night. So he entered the house as one angered, and they began clearing their throats and making noise until he came out to them and said: "O people, take upon yourselves of deeds what you are able to bear, for Allah does not tire of reward until you tire of deeds, and the best of deeds is that which is most constant, even if it is little" [42] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/37.]]. Then there was revealed to him: ﴿O you who wrap yourself in garments! Stand [in prayer] through the night﴾, and it was made obligatory upon them and made like an obligation, so that one of them would tie a rope and hold onto it. They remained for eight months. When Allah saw what they were being burdened with, and what they sought by it, the face of Allah and His pleasure, He had mercy on them and lifted it from them, and said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it﴾, to the end of the verse. Thus He returned them to the obligation and lifted from them the night prayer except what they undertook voluntarily.

Al-Hasan said: In this verse, the "praise be to Allah" is a voluntary act after an obligation.

﴿And recite the Qur'an distinctly.﴾ Al-Hasan said: Recite it with deliberate recitation, make its clarity clear. Also from him: Recite it at your ease, three verses, four, and five. Qatadah: Be steadfast in it. Ibn Kaysan: Understand it while reciting it. It was said: Explain it in detail and do not hasten in its recitation; this is from the saying of the Arabs: thaghghara ratl and ratl when the teeth are spaced. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir: Reflect upon the subtleties of His address, demand of yourself acting upon its rulings, your heart understanding its meanings, and your inner self turning toward it.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us from Sufyan, from Asim, from Zirr, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It will be said to the companion of the Qur'an: Recite and ascend, and recite distinctly as you used to recite in the world, for your station will be at the last verse you recite" [43] [[Fath al-Bari: 13/349; al-Sunan al-Kubra: 5/22, no. 8056.]].

﴿Indeed, We shall cast upon you a heavy word.﴾ Al-Hasan said: A man may study the surah, but acting upon it is heavy.

Qatadah said: Heavy, by Allah, are its obligations and limits. Ibn Abbas: severe. Abu al-Aliyah: heavy with promise and threat, the lawful and the unlawful. Muhammad ibn Ka'b: heavy upon the hypocrites. Al-Farra': ﴿heavy﴾, not light and worthless, because it is the speech of our Lord. Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya: awe-inspiring; from this one says of an intelligent man: he is dignified and weighty.

I heard the teacher Abu al-Qayyim ibn Jundab say: I heard Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Mudarib ibn Ibrahim say: I heard al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl, when asked about this verse, say: its meaning is: ﴿Indeed, We shall cast upon you a word﴾ light upon the tongue, ﴿heavy﴾ in the scale. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir said: He means a word that none carries except a heart supported by success and a soul adorned with monotheism. Al-Qayyim said: In this verse, hearing knowledge from a scholar is bitter, and acting upon it is heavy, but it brings joy when the servant acts upon it with the earnestness of the Sunnah and perfect manners. It was also said: He means that the Qur'an is heavy for its bearer. Ibn Zayd said: By Allah, it is heavy and blessed, just as it was heavy in this world it will be heavy in the scales on the Day of Resurrection.

Abu al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Fadl al-Qahandari informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: and in what I read to Abdullah, from Malik, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, that al-Harith ibn Hisham asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: O Messenger of Allah, how does revelation come to you? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and it is the hardest upon me; then it departs from me, and I have retained what it said. And sometimes the angel appears to me as a man, and I understand what he says" [44] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/158; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/39.]].

Aisha said: I saw him when it was revealed to him on a very cold day, and it departed from him, and his forehead was dripping with sweat.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Abdi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Najdah narrated to us, saying: Yahya al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, who said: Revelation would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was on his mount, and its weight would press upon it.

﴿Indeed, the rising of the night﴾ — that is, all its hours; every hour of it is nashi'ah, named so because it arises (tansha'u), and from it comes "the cloud arose" (nasha'at al-sahabah) when it appears; Allah creates it, and its plural is nashi'at.

Aqil informed me, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Ibn Jarir informed us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to me, saying:

Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Hatim ibn Safirah informed us, saying: I said to Abd ibn Abi Mulaykah: Will you not tell me which part of the night is nashi'ah? He said: You have fallen upon a sure matter. I asked Ibn Abbas about it, and he claimed that the whole night is nashi'ah. I asked Ibn al-Zubayr about it, and he told me the same. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd said: Any hour in which one rises in the night has risen, and in the language of Abyssinia nashi'a means to rise. Ikrimah said: Whatever you stand for at the beginning of the night is nashi'ah.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Majah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Sayyar narrated to us, saying: Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Jarir, from some of his shaykhs, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, that he would pray between Maghrib and Isha and say: Have you not heard the words of Allah, glorified is He: "Indeed, the rising of the night"? This is the rising of the night.

Abu Mijlaz and Qatadah said: Whatever is after Isha is nashi'ah. Ubayd ibn Umayr said: I said to Aisha: A man who stood in prayer at the beginning of the night, is he called one who stood in nashi'ah? She said: No; nashi'ah is only standing after sleep. Yaman and Ibn Kaysan said: It is standing at the end of the night.

﴿It is firmer in tread (wat'an)﴾ — Abu Amr, Ibn Amir and Ibn Mahisn read wiṭa' with a kasra on the waw and with a long vowel, and Abu Ubayd preferred it in the sense of harmony and agreement, that the heart, hearing and sight agree with the tongue. The rest read with a fatha on the waw and short vowel, meaning emptiness of the heart. Ibn Abbas said: Their prayers were at the beginning of the night, ﴿it is firmer in tread﴾, meaning it is more fitting that you comprehend what Allah has prescribed upon you of standing in prayer, because when a person sleeps he does not know when he will awake.

Qatadah said: More steadfast in goodness, more retentive for recitation. Al-Farra': more steadfast in standing. Al-Qurtubi: harder upon the one praying than daytime prayer, as evidenced by the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "O Allah, make Your tread heavy upon Mudar" [45].

Ibn Zayd: It empties the heart more than the day, because no needs or anything else come upon him. Al-Hasan: ﴿firmer in tread﴾ in goodness and more protective from Satan.

﴿And more upright in speech﴾ — more correct in recitation; and the worship of the night is more energetic, more complete in sincerity, and more abundant in blessing.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 73, verses 7–20:**

*"Indeed, for you by day is extended occupation (sabhan tawilan)."* The recitation of the common readers is with an unpointed ḥāʾ (sabḥan), meaning free time and space for your sleep and for attending to your needs. The root meaning of sabḥ is swift movement, from which comes swimming in water (al-sibāḥa) and a swift-running horse (faras sābiḥ). A poet said:

*"They have permitted you the eastern and western lands, so in them, my friend, there is ample room (sabḥ) for you."*

Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read *sabkhan* with a pointed khāʾ, meaning lightness, space and rest. From this is the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying to ʿĀʾisha when she invoked curses upon a thief who had stolen from her: "Do not lighten (lā tasabbikhī) him by your supplication against him."

[46] That is, do not lighten. *Al-tasbīkh* is the loosening and fluffing of cotton and wool. It is said to a woman, "Fluff (sabbikhī) your cotton," and the pieces of cotton when they are carded are called *sābikh*.

al-Akhṭal, describing the hunter and the dogs, said:

*"They released them, scattering the dust as one scatters carded cotton fluffed by the bowstring."* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/43.]]

Tha'lab said: *al-sabḥ* is restlessness and agitation, while *al-sabkh* is stillness. From this is the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Fever is from the heat of Hell, so cool it (fa-sabbikhūhā) with water."

[47] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/43.]] That is, calm it.

*"And mention the name of your Lord"*: with tawḥīd and exaltation. Sahl said: "Recite *In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate*, at the beginning of your prayers, and its blessing, by its recitation, will connect them to your Lord and cut you off from everything other than Him."

*"And devote yourself to Him with complete devotion"*: Ibn ʿAbbās and most people said: sincerely devote yourself to Him in sincerity. al-Ḥasan said: strive. Ibn Zayd said: be free for His worship. Shaqīq said: rely upon Him completely.

I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Sulamī say: I heard Manṣūr ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: I heard Abū al-Qayyim al-Bazzāz say: Ibn ʿAtāʾ said: "Cut yourself off to Him, a complete cutting off," and this is the root of this matter. It is said: *battaltu al-shayʾ*, meaning I cut the thing off. *Ṣadaqa battatun battalatun* means a charity that is irrevocable and cut off from its giver, with no claim left to him over it. *Dār tabtīl* means a house cut off from other houses. Imru' al-Qays said:

*"She lights up the darkness at nightfall like a lamp of a monk who has withdrawn (mutabattil) at evening."*

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade *tabattul* (celibate withdrawal). From this root Mary is called *al-Batūl*, the virgin.

Abū al-Qayyim said: "He connected himself to Him with a connection; none who reached it turned back except from the path. No one reached it and then turned away from it."

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī said: "Raise the hands in prayer."

Zayd ibn Aslam said: *tabattul* is renouncing the world and all that is in it, and seeking what is with God. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/44.]]

*"Lord of the East and the West"*: the people of the Ḥijāz, Abū ʿAmr, Ayyūb and Ḥafṣ read *rabbu* with a *ḍamma* on the bāʾ, as a new subject (mubtadaʾ). It is also said that it is by assuming a hidden *huwa* (He). The rest read it with a *kasra*, as a qualifier (naʿt) of "your Lord" in His saying, "And mention the name of your Lord," and so on.

*"There is no god but He, so take Him as your trustee (wakīl)"*: a guardian over your affairs; so entrust your affairs to Him. *"And bear patiently what they say, and abandon them with graceful abandonment."* This was abrogated by the verse of fighting.

al-Ḥasan told me: al-Sunnī narrated to us, saying: Ḥātim ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, saying: Suraych ibn Yūnus narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Muḥammad al-Warrāq narrated to us, from al-Aḥwaṣ ibn Ḥakīm, from his father, from Abū al-Zāhiriyya, that Abū al-Dardāʾ said: "We frown at the faces of some people and smile at them, while our hearts curse them, or they curse them."

*"Leave Me with those who deny, the people of plenty, and give them respite for a little while."* It was revealed concerning the chiefs of Quraysh, the notorious deniers. Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: it was revealed concerning those who fed (the army) at Badr, who were ten, whom we mentioned in al-Anfāl. *Al-niʿma* is luxury and comfort, and also favor and kindness. *Al-niʿma* with a *ḍamma* on the nūn means ease and prosperity. It is said: *niʿm* and *niʿma*, a fresh spring, and *niʿmā*, a fresh eye.

*"Indeed with Us are shackles (ankālan)"*: heavy fetters with Us in the Hereafter, which will never be loosened. Its singular is *nikl*. al-Shaʿbī said: "Do you think God makes the shackles on the feet of the people of the Fire because He feared they would flee? No, but when He wants them to rise, He will pull them down upon them." *"And a blazing fire, and food that chokes, and a painful punishment"*: food that catches in the throat, neither going down nor coming out. It is al-Ghislīn, al-Zaqqūm and al-Ḍarīʿ.

ʿAqīl told me that Abū al-Faraj informed them, from Ibn Jarīr, who said: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Ḥamza al-Zayyāt, from Ḥamrān ibn Aʿyan, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited, "Indeed with Us are shackles and a blazing fire and food that chokes," and fainted.

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Ibn Māja narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn Ayyūb narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ziyād narrated to us, saying: Sayyār narrated to us, saying: Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Khālid ibn Ḥassān narrated to us, saying: "al-Ḥasan came to us in the evening, and he was fasting. We brought him food, and this verse, *Indeed with Us are shackles and a blazing fire and food that chokes and a painful punishment*, was recited before him. He said: 'Remove the food.' On the second night we brought him food again, and this verse was recited before him, and he said: 'Remove it.' On the third night I came to him, and this verse was recited before him, and he said: 'Remove it.' His son went to Thābit al-Bunānī, Yazīd al-Ḍabbī and Yaḥyā al-Bakkāʾ and told them his story. They came with him and kept at him until he drank a sip of barley drink (sawīq)."

*"On the day the earth and the mountains quake"*: that is, they will move and be shaken with those upon them. *"And the mountains will become a heap of sand (kathīban), poured out (mahīlan)"*: the sand that is gathered, flowing and scattering when it is touched and crumbles. Its origin is *mahyūl*, a passive form from the saying, "I poured the sand, so I pour it," which is when its base is moved and it collapses from above upon itself. It is said: *mahīl* and *mahyūl*, *mukīl* and *makyūl*, *maʿīn* and *maʿyūn*.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions when they complained of drought: "Do you measure (atakīlūn) or pour out (tuhīlūn)?"

They said: "We pour out."

He said: "Measure and do not pour out."[48] [[al-Fāʾiq fī Gharīb al-Ḥadīth: 3/416.]]

A poet said:

*"I think you are a lord who is envied (maʿyūn)."* [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 6/2171.]]

*"Indeed We have sent to you a messenger, a witness against you, as We sent a messenger to Pharaoh. But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a severe seizing (akhdhan wabīlan)."* Heavy, difficult, burdensome. From it comes the saying, "a pasture that is *mustawbil*," and "food that is *mustawbal*" when it is not digested, and from it comes *al-wabāl* (ruin). al-Khansāʾ said:

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions when they complained of drought: "Do you measure (atakīlūn) or pour out (tuhīlūn)?"

They said: "We pour out."

He said: "Measure and do not pour out."[48] [[al-Fāʾiq fī Gharīb al-Ḥadīth: 3/416.]]

A poet said:

*"I think you are a lord who is envied (maʿyūn)."* [[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 6/2171.]]

*"Indeed We have sent to you a messenger, a witness against you, as We sent a messenger to Pharaoh. But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a severe seizing (akhdhan wabīlan)."* Heavy, difficult, burdensome. From it comes the saying, "a pasture that is *mustawbil*," and "food that is *mustawbal*" when it is not digested, and from it comes *al-wabāl* (ruin). al-Khansāʾ said:

*"Bujayla has eaten greatly (akalan wabīlan) on the day it met the horsemen of Mālik."* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/49.]]

The Arabs say: "The purchase has been *awbala* upon him," meaning it has been followed up (repeated).

*"Then how will you guard yourselves (fa-kayfa tattaqūna) if you disbelieve?"* That is, how will you have piety on the Day of Resurrection if you disbelieve in this world? That is: you will have no way to piety, and piety will not benefit you when you reach the Resurrection. It is also said that the meaning is: how will you guard yourselves against the punishment of a day, and how will you be saved from it, if you disbelieve? Ibn Masʿūd and ʿAṭiyya read: *fa-kayfa yattaqūna yawman yajʿalu al-wildāna shīban in kafartum* (how will they guard themselves against a day that makes the children gray-haired, if you disbelieve).

Abū al-Simmāk al-ʿAdawī read *yattaqūna* with a *kasra* on the nūn, as an idāfa (construct).

*"A day that makes the children (al-wildān), the youths, gray-haired (shīban)"*: white-haired from its terror and severity. That is when it is said to Adam: "Stand and send forth the army of the Fire from your offspring."

al-Ḥasan told me: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn Abī al-Khaṭīb narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ghālib told me, saying: I heard ʿUthmān ibn al-Haytham say: "I passed by Ibn al-Sarrī while he was standing in the road, and a man asked him about *a day that makes the children gray-haired*. He said: 'They are the children of fornication.'"

It is also said: they are the children of polytheists.

*"The sky will be split (munfaṭir)"*, that is, rent and cracked, *"because of it. His promise was ever fulfilled."* *"Indeed this (sūra, or these verses) is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way"* by faith and obedience.

*"Indeed your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) nearer than two-thirds of the night."* Hishām narrated from the people of Syria *thulthay* with light, unemphatic pronunciation. *"And half of it, and a third of it"*: the people of Mecca and Kufa read these in the accusative, meaning "and you stand half of it and a third of it." The rest read them in the genitive, as coordinated with *thulthay*. *"And a group of those with you"* also stands in prayer.

*"And God measures the night and the day. He knew that you would not be able to keep count (tuḥṣūhu)"*, that is, you would not be able to sustain the night prayer. *"So He turned to you in forgiveness"*: He overlooked you and turned back to you, lightening the burden upon you. *"So recite what is easy of the Qur'an."* al-Suddī said: "A hundred verses." al-Ḥasan said: "Whoever recites a hundred verses in his night will not be disputed with by the Qur'an." Kaʿb said: "Whoever recites a hundred verses in his night is written among the devout (al-qānitīn)." Saʿīd said: "Fifty verses." al-Rabīʿ ibn Ṣabīḥ narrated from al-Ḥasan: *fa-iqrāʾū mā tayassara minhu*, and he said: "That is, in the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers."

*"He knew that there would be among you the sick, and others traveling through the land seeking of God's bounty, and others fighting in the way of God."* He equated the rank of the fighters with those who earn lawful wealth to spend on themselves and their dependents, and for kindness and generosity.

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Ibn Salm narrated to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Khāliq narrated to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Fatḥ told me, saying: Abū Naṣr Bishr ibn al-Ḥarith said: al-Muʿāfā ibn ʿImrān and ʿIsā ibn Yūnus narrated to us, from Farqad al-Sabakhī, from Ibrāhīm, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: "Any man who brings goods into a city of the cities of the Muslims, patiently seeking reward, and sells them at that day's price, will have with God the rank of the martyrs." Then ʿAbd Allāh recited: *and others traveling through the land seeking of God's bounty, and others fighting in the way of God.*

Ibn Fanjawayh also told me: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿAqīl narrated to us, from al-Qayyim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from his father, who said: "I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: 'God has created no death that I would die after being killed in the way of God more beloved to me than dying between the two wings of a man who is traveling through the land seeking of God's bounty.'"

*"So recite what is easy of it."*

I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Sulamī say: I heard Manṣūr ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: I heard Abū al-Qayyim al-Iskandarānī say: I heard Abū Jaʿfar al-Malaṭī say: from ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā, from his father, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, concerning this verse, he said: "*What is easy for you of it* is humility of the heart and purity of the inner self."[49] [[Tafsir Majmaʿ al-Bayān: 10/169.]]

*"And establish the prayer, and give the zakat, and lend God a goodly loan. Whatever good you send forward for yourselves, you will find it with God, better and greater in reward"*, than what you would have sent forward had you not sent it. Here *khayran* and *aʿẓama* are in the accusative as the second object. The *huwa* between them is, according to the Basrans, a separator (faṣl), and according to the Kufans, a support (ʿimād) with no grammatical position (lā maḥalla lahu min al-iʿrāb). *"And seek God's forgiveness. Indeed God is Forgiving, Merciful."*
